get.description: BackOffice-authenticated keyset listing of one user's time entries in one workspace. view=logged lists entries with logged time (ordered by start desc); view=planned lists entries with planned time (ordered by planned_start desc). An entry carrying both appears in both views. Deliberately historical: entries remain listed after the user leaves the workspace. Pagination is cursor-based so a delete between pages cannot make rows drift past the reader: follow next_cursor to walk older and prev_cursor to walk newer, stopping when the one you follow is null. Data is always newest-first. The total lives on the sibling /count endpoint because it depends only on the filters.

get.description: Returns the time off of the given organization users with personal detail stripped: each entry carries only its id, the user it belongs to, and the start and end of the period — no category and no audit timestamps. Available to any member of the organization. `user_id` is required and repeatable, and so is the `start_date`/`end_date` window; both are dates (YYYY-MM-DD), interpreted in UTC, and `end_date` is inclusive of that whole day. An entry is returned when its period overlaps the window at either edge, so an entry that starts before `start_date` or ends after `end_date` is still included.
get.summary: Get time offs of organization users

get.description: Returns the full time off entries of one organization user, including the category and the creation and last-modification timestamps. Requires the `manage_time_off` organization permission — this applies to reading as well, and to a caller's own entries. The `from`/`to` window is required; both are dates (YYYY-MM-DD), interpreted in UTC, and `to` is inclusive of that whole day. An entry is returned when its period overlaps the window at either edge, so an entry that starts before `from` or ends after `to` is still included.
get.summary: Get time off for organization user

put.description: Updates one or more existing time off entries of the specified user in a single call. The request body is an array: each element identifies the entry by its `timeoff_id` and carries the new `start_time` and `end_time` (RFC3339) plus an optional `type`. Every element replaces the entry in full, so omitting `type` clears the entry's existing category rather than leaving it unchanged — resend the current value to keep it. Include each `timeoff_id` at most once: with duplicates, which element wins is undefined. Elements whose `timeoff_id` does not match an entry of the user are skipped. All elements are applied in a single transaction: if applying them would leave any two of the user's approved or pending time off entries overlapping (entries created through this API are approved), the whole request fails with a 409 and nothing is updated. Requires the `manage_time_off` organization permission. Responds 200 with the entries that were actually updated.
put.summary: Update time off for the specified user

409.description: Overlapping time off entry

post.description: Creates one or more time off entries for the specified user in a single call. The request body is an array: each element needs a `start_time` and an `end_time` (RFC3339) and may carry an optional `type`. All elements are created in a single transaction: a period that overlaps one of the user's approved or pending time off entries — or another element of the same request — fails the whole request with a 409 and nothing is created (entries created through this API are approved). Requires the `manage_time_off` organization permission. Responds 200 with the created entries, each including the id it was assigned.
post.summary: Create time off for the specified user

409.description: Overlapping time off entry

delete.description: Deletes one or more time off entries of the specified user. The request body is an array of time off ids. Ids that do not match an entry of the user are skipped silently — the response does not indicate how many entries were deleted. Requires the `manage_time_off` organization permission. Responds 204 with no body.
delete.summary: Delete time off for the specified user

get.description:
Returns working minutes plus gross and remaining scheduled estimates for each requested user or resource.
'estimated_minutes' is gross timeline work from non-draft task estimates, projected recurring tasks, and planned calendar events.
When 'include_drafts' is true, 'estimated_minutes' also includes task estimates from draft projects.
'estimated_remaining_minutes' nets each assignee's tracked time and places unfinished work from workspace-local today.
Placement uses future working days. Weekends and public holidays are excluded.
Past and overdue task slices are zero; planned events count only from today.

post.description: Starts the asynchronous Cadence workflow that parses CSV files into NDJSON and imports entities tier-by-tier (custom field definitions, clients, projects, tags, users, tasks, time entries). The upload must be in "mapping" status, or already "importing" for idempotent retries. Uses a deterministic workflow ID so retries are safe. Poll GET /uploads/{request_id} for progress and final status. In every mode, a user the managers column names who is already a plain member of that project is promoted to project manager, and nobody is ever demoted — so re-running an import can change existing people's roles, and revert does not undo it. Set match_existing_only=true to import in match-only mode: clients, projects, tasks, and users are matched against existing rows and never created — unmatched clients/projects/tasks and unmatched users (never invited) are skipped, along with the time entries depending on them; custom field definitions are neither created nor extended in this mode, so every field-catalog row is skipped. A matched project is still updated from its row (custom field values merged, tags linked, members/managers granted, billable set when the cell has a value), and so is a matched task (custom field values merged, tags linked, assignees added, and description/estimated_minutes/start_date/end_date/billable set when the cell has a value — archived is create-only, since archiving has to cascade to subtasks and time entries); those updates are not undone by revert. A project match covers archived, completed and inactive projects but never a recurring template, and a name+client several live projects share (recurring instances, for example) is skipped with a warning rather than written to whichever one the database returned first. A task match is refused the same way: a name several live tasks share under the same project and parent is skipped, and so is a task belonging to a recurring series, whose every future instance would otherwise inherit the row's values. A project or task the import wrote to is reported under stats.projects.updated / stats.tasks.updated rather than matched, so the summary separates the rows that changed from the ones that were only found.

match_existing_only.description:
MatchExistingOnly switches the import into match-only mode: clients,
projects, tasks, and users are matched against existing rows and never
created. Unmatched structural rows — and the time entries that depend on
them — are skipped instead of creating new entities. Users are matched
against existing workspace members only and never invited; a time entry
whose user isn't an existing member is skipped rather than routed to the
importing user. Time entries whose task and user are matched are still
imported onto the existing task.
Client and project names match exactly (case- and whitespace-sensitive),
while task names match case- and whitespace-insensitively; check the
casing of skipped client/project rows before re-uploading.

A project match covers archived, completed and inactive projects, not only
the ones visible in the default project list — so a row can update a
project an admin no longer thinks of as live. Recurring templates are the
one exception: they are never matched, because a write to a template is
inherited by every instance created from it afterwards.

A matched project is still updated from its row: custom field values are
merged in (values the CSV doesn't map are preserved), tags are linked,
members and managers are granted — an existing member listed as a manager
is promoted, and nobody is ever demoted — and billable is set when the row
carries a value, left alone when the cell is blank or the column unmapped.
The project's client binding is never changed. Linking a tag that doesn't
exist yet creates that tag; nothing else is created. These updates are NOT
reverted by the revert endpoint, which only removes rows the import
created.

A matched task is updated from its row the same way: custom field values
are merged in, tags are linked, assignees are added — never removed — and
description, estimated_minutes, start_date, end_date and billable are each
written when the row carries a value and left alone when the cell is blank
or the column unmapped. The task's project, client and parent bindings are
never changed. archived is the one mapped task column this mode does not
apply: archiving a task has to cascade to its subtasks and time entries,
which an import cannot do at CSV scale, so the column is read only when a
task is created. Like the project updates, none of this is reverted.

Two task matches this mode refuses to write to, skipping the row with a
warning rather than guessing: a name that several live tasks share under
the same project and parent, and a task belonging to a recurring series.
The series parent carries the recurrence rule and every instance the
generator creates afterwards inherits its description, estimate, dates,
tags, assignees and custom field values, so one row would reshape the whole
future series with no way to undo it.

A matched client stays untouched, since its row carries only its name,
which is the match key.

A matched user is not invited, but a mapped role column IS applied to
them: their Focus role in this workspace is changed to the one the row
names, and their roles in other products are left as they are.
Organization admins and the account running the import are skipped. Unlike
the project and task updates above, this one IS reverted — the previous
role is saved before the change and put back by the revert endpoint.

A field-catalog import (the custom_field entity) has no matching behavior
to fall back to — it either creates fields and options or it doesn't —
so this mode skips every custom_field row outright, with no fields
created and no options added to existing fields.

name.description:
Name is omitted for failures with no entity name (e.g. a blank/unmapped

match_existing_only.description:
MatchExistingOnly previews a match-only import: unmatched clients,
projects, tasks, and users are reported as would-be-skipped instead of
would-create (users are never invited), while a matched project's or task's
row values are validated for warnings. See ConfirmRequest.MatchExistingOnly.

computed_at.description: ComputedAt is set by the finalize activity when the dry-run completes.

counts.description:
Counts holds per entity type: total / created (would-create) / updated
(would write to an existing row) / matched (reused existing, untouched) /
skipped (dropped — unmatched + create-new disabled) / failed, mirroring
the import-time Stats shape. See EntityStats.

failures.description:
Failures is a capped sample of rows that would be skipped or fail, each
categorized (see DryRunFailure* constants) so the UI can separate fixable
CSV issues from transient DB errors.

mapping_hash.description:
MappingHash is the fingerprint of the effective inputs this result was
computed against. The API compares it to the upload's current hash to flag
a result as stale after the mapping changes. The mode toggle below is
intentionally excluded from the hash — it changes counts but not the
underlying data — so it's surfaced separately for the FE to compare against
the user's current selection.

match_existing_only.description:
MatchExistingOnly records the mode this result was computed in. The FE
re-runs when the user's current toggle differs, since the counts (created
vs would-be-skipped) only hold for the mode they were computed in.

successes.description:
Successes is a capped sample of rows a real import would create, update or
match, so the preview can show a sample of the data being imported
alongside the flagged rows in Failures — not just the errors. They carry
no reason; the FE renders them with a status column driven by Status.

entity.description:
Entity is the plural JSON entity name (clients, projects, tasks, tags,
users, teams, time_entries, custom_fields, project_rates,
project_member_rates, member_rates, member_costs, member_working_hours,
member_roles, member_rate_segments, member_cost_segments), stamped by the
aggregator
like DryRunFailure.Entity.

name.description:
Name is the entity name (email for users). Omitted for rows with no name
of their own (e.g. a time entry).

row.description:
Row is the 1-based CSV source line, matching DryRunFailure.Row. Omitted (0)
when the line isn't known.

status.description:
Status is the would-be outcome: created (net-new), updated (existing row
written to) or matched (reused existing, untouched). See DryRunRowCreated /
DryRunRowUpdated / DryRunRowMatched.

member_rate_segments.description:
MemberRateSegments and MemberCostSegments count the TIMELINE path: several
rows assembling one member's rate or cost history. Deliberately separate
from MemberRates and MemberCosts above, which count the single-cell
user.rate and user.cost path. Same table on the backend, but one writes a
segment effective today and the other replaces a whole history, so a
combined count would describe neither. The FE sums each pair into one card
because an admin reading a total does not care which mapping produced it.

member_roles.description:
MemberRoles counts workspace role changes applied to members who already
exist. Separate from Users, which counts the invites: a role change writes
to somebody the import did not create, so folding it into Users would tell
an admin they invited people they did not.

created.description: Created is net-new rows (would-create in a dry-run).

failed.description: Failed is rows that errored (validation / DB).

matched.description: Matched is rows reused from an existing entity found by key — no write.

options_added.description:
OptionsAdded is custom_field-only: select options the import wrote onto
fields it matched rather than created. It counts options, not rows — the
rows themselves are the custom_field entries in Updated — so it is the
only field here outside the total identity. In a dry-run it reads as
would-add, the same way Created does. Zero for every other entity type.
Counts only options this import actually wrote: one that turned out to
already exist (a concurrent writer won the race) leaves the row Matched
but is not counted here.

skipped.description:
Skipped is rows dropped because their entity/dependency wasn't found and
create-new is disabled (match-existing-only mode). Distinct from Matched:
these are not imported. Enumerated in DryRunResult.Failures. custom_field
rows are also Skipped (never Failed) for expected creation blockers —
beta disabled, workspace field-slot ceiling reached — since the row's
own data isn't at fault; those carry DryRunFailureSkippedByPolicy so a
skip stays identifiable outside match-existing-only mode.

updated.description:
Updated is rows that matched an existing entity the import then wrote to:
a match-existing-only project whose billable/custom-field values were
applied, a match-existing-only task whose scalars or custom-field values
were applied, an adopted project/task/client (the integration linkage is
stamped), a re-imported row whose custom-field merge altered the blob, a
matched custom field that gained select options, or a rate row whose
timeline was rewritten. Disjoint from Matched — a row is never both.

Counts real writes: a value identical to what is already stored leaves the
row Matched. The match-existing-only preview diffs the row against the
entity it matched (task.ImportUpdateWouldChange /
project.ImportUpdateWouldChange) and predicts the same way, so re-running
an already-imported file previews as Matched rather than Updated. It stays
a prediction: a row edited between the preview and the confirm lands on
whatever the write's own guard decides.

The other tiers still predict from whether the row carries anything to
write, so their preview count remains an upper bound: normal-mode custom
field merges, matched custom fields gaining options, and the rate tiers,
where the preview reads no timelines at all and reports every surviving
rate row as a would-create.

Always serialised (no omitempty), so a response carrying stats always
carries this. It is schema-optional only because marking it required would
break every generated client that already builds an EntityStats.

default_start_time.description:
HH:MM. Used when a time_entry start lacks a time component or is
missing entirely. Empty falls back to "09:00" UTC.

custom_fields.description:
CustomFields is the per-workspace list of importable custom field
targets. Populated only in API responses; empty in the static registry.

can_invite_members.description:
CanInviteMembers mirrors the field on UploadResponse so a resumed or
reloaded wizard can re-derive it — the FE store is in-memory, so without
this the warning silently disappears on refresh and the admin confirms
into the failed rows it exists to prevent. Resolved for the user making
*this* request, not the one who uploaded.

Nil means "not computed": the list endpoint shares this struct and
answering it per row would cost one authz call each. Treat nil as unknown
rather than as false.

dry_run_status.description:
Dry-run state. DryRunStatus is "" until the first dry-run runs.
DryRunStale is true when a completed result was computed against a mapping
that has since changed — the FE should re-run before showing the confirm
summary.

unsettable_fields.description:
UnsettableFields mirrors the field on UploadResponse so a resumed wizard
re-derives it for the user making *this* request. Nil means not computed
(the list endpoint shares this struct); treat that as unknown, not as
"everything is settable".

can_invite_members.description:
CanInviteMembers reports whether this admin may add people who are not
already in the organization. False means the import can still update
members it matches, but every new email would be rejected — so the UI
should say so while the mapping is still being built, rather than letting
the admin discover it from a page of failed rows after confirming.

unsettable_fields.description:
UnsettableFields names the qualified targets ("user.rate") this admin
lacks the permission to write, so the mapping screen can disable them with
a reason instead of accepting a column that the import then drops.

A list rather than a flag per field: the set grows with every
permission-gated attribute, and a caller that does not recognise an entry
can ignore it. CanInviteMembers stays separate because it is not a field —
it decides whether members can be created at all, which is the mode
toggle, not a column.

Empty means everything mappable is settable, which is the common case.

ordered_ids.description:
max=100 mirrors the per-field option cap. ordered_ids may list a subset of the
active options (the rest keep their current order), so unlike field reorder it
isn't coupled to a full active set.

max=50 must stay in sync with constants.MaxCFSlots: ordered_ids carries
the full active set, which create caps at MaxCFSlots per entity_type, so a
lower bound here would make full workspaces un-reorderable. Struct tags
can't reference Go constants; TestReorderPayloadCapMatchesMaxCFSlots guards
the coupling.

period_start.description: PeriodStart is the recurring project period's first day.

projection_revision.description: ProjectionRevision identifies the projected period version.

virtual.description: Virtual indicates the entry is an unmaterialized recurring task.

weight.description:
The weight of a task in the timeline. This is not unique, and one or more
tasks may have the same weight as long as their dates do not conflict.

best_streak.description:
BestStreak (db column best_streak) is the durable peak streak length ever reached,
folded in at consolidation time from bestStreakInWindow's scan of the loaded warehouse
window (see models.go). It is monotonic (persisted via GREATEST), so it survives a
broken chain that resets PreviousStreak/Streak -- unlike those, a comparison change DOES
reset it (service.Update), since the achieved flags it was computed from are no longer
comparable under the new comparison. The read path (fetchAndFoldGoalStats) returns
max(stored BestStreak, current window peak) so a peak from the still-visible window is
reflected even before the next consolidation run persists it.

is_syncing.description:
IsSyncing is true while the warehouse has not yet reflected the goal's latest
configuration or activity, and clients should treat CurrentRecurrence's tracked time as
stale/pending rather than a settled zero. This covers two cases: (1) a materialised
current period whose synced_at lags content_updated_at (a config edit is still being
recomputed), and (2) a period that has never been materialised on a goal created within
the last few minutes, but only when the current date falls within the goal's active
window and the synthesised period is one the warehouse can actually generate (the async
post-create warehouse refresh hasn't run yet). Past that initial window, or when no
materialisable period exists at all (e.g. a future start_date), a never-materialised
period is a true zero, not a pending sync.

last_completed_recurrence_start_date.description:
LastCompletedRecurrenceStartDate is newer than the sibling EndDate field above and, unlike
it, is marked optional (binding:"optional", x-nullable) so existing FE consumers built
against the swagger schema before this field existed don't need a lockstep update just to
keep tsc green -- this is an additive field, not a required one.

periods_met.description:
PeriodsMet/PeriodsTotal power the Goals page "N of M periods met" success-rate KPI.
PeriodsMet = ConsolidatedPeriodsMet + achieved visible completed rows, clamped to
PeriodsTotal (transient ETL/timezone states can briefly disagree with the Go calendar
math). PeriodsTotal is pure Go calendar math (see recurrence.go), not a warehouse read,
since warehouse rows behind the anchor are physically deleted.

position.description:
Position is a per-(workspace_id, toggl_user_id) zero-based list ordering, controlled
entirely by the FE via the reorder endpoint. It is bookkeeping, not user-facing content:
changing it must never bump ContentUpdatedAt (see the denylist in
goal_set_content_updated_at.sql), since that field drives IsSyncing and the warehouse
drift probe, and a visual-only reorder has nothing to reconcile.
Intentionally excluded from the generic metadata-update path (internal/goal/sql/update.sql
does not write this column) -- only create (append-to-end) and reorder (explicit
reordering) may change it, to avoid a race where a concurrent Reorder's new position is
silently reverted by an in-flight Update that read the goal's old position.

week_start_on.description:
WeekStartOn (db column week_start_on) snapshots the weekday (0=Sunday, 1=Monday) a
weekly goal's periods align to, captured at creation time from StartDate. It is
immutable thereafter, unlike the user's own settings.StartWeekOn (db column
start_week_on on user_settings -- note the transposed name), so toggling that setting
later cannot desync the warehouse materialization from the streak anchor
(toggl/ic-tribe#1887). NULL for non-weekly goals and for weekly goals created before
this column existed.

custom_field_values.description:

don't hydrate (e.g. timeentry) leave the slice empty; omitempty
hides it on those responses.

rollover_mins.description:
RolloverMins is the cumulative under/over budget carried into this
instance from earlier instances in its recurring chain, in minutes.
Positive = surplus (prior periods went under estimate, time carries
forward); negative = debt (prior periods went over). Only populated
for recurring instances; nil for templates and standalone projects.
See service.HydrateRollover for the per-instance contribution rules
driven by RolloverMode (expire / carry_over / carry_all).

the effective tags fall through to the linked task's tags. A non-nil

current_layer.description:
CurrentLayer is the layer that must act next for the timesheet to
advance. On submission it is 0 (waiting on the lowest approver layer).
After the approver at the current layer approves, it advances to the
next configured layer. Setup validation requires approver layers to be
contiguous from 0, so in practice that next layer is N+1; the traversal
(nextLayerAfter) nonetheless does not assume contiguity. The timesheet
reaches Status=approved when no higher configured layer remains to act.

When an approver at layer N requests changes, status becomes
changes_requested with CurrentLayer=N. On resubmit, status
returns to submitted with CurrentLayer=N — the chain restarts at
the rejecting layer rather than at 0, preserving earlier-layer
approvals.

from all read and materialisation paths. Set by the per-member

submitter_timezone.description:

submission time. Used so approvers see the member's data in the
member's local time even if the member later changes timezone.

from active queries and no new periods are generated for it.

email_reminder_enabled.description:
EmailReminderEnabled gates the pending-reminder email channel for this
setup. When false (the default) the reminder cron skips this setup's
members even if ReminderDay/ReminderTime are set.

end_date.description:
EndDate is set when the setup is discontinued. While nil, the setup
continues to generate periods indefinitely. When set, no new periods
are generated past this date.

period_days.description:
PeriodDays is the length of a period in days. Required (and minimum 1)
when Periodicity == PeriodicityDays. Must be nil otherwise.

periodicity.description:
Periodicity defines the cadence of the timesheet periods.
See the Periodicity constants for valid values.

reminder_day.description:
ReminderDay defines when in the period a reminder is sent to members
who haven't submitted yet. Interpretation depends on Periodicity:
  - weekly:  0..6 (0 = Sunday)
  - monthly: 1..31 (clamps to month length)
  - days:    number of days into the period
Reminders are not sent when ReminderDay or ReminderTime is nil.

reminder_time.description:
ReminderTime is the wall-clock time the reminder is sent, formatted
HH:MM, interpreted in each member's own timezone (resolved when the
reminder cron runs; UTC when the member's timezone is unknown).
Reminders are not sent when ReminderDay or ReminderTime is nil.

start_date.description:
StartDate is the anchor for period computation and the inclusive start
of the very first period. All subsequent period boundaries derive
from this date plus the periodicity rule.

updated_at.description: UpdatedAt tracks the last mutation. Nil for never-updated rows.

workspace_id.description: WorkspaceID is the workspace this setup belongs to.

created_at.description: CreatedAt is the row creation timestamp.

deleted_at.description:
DeletedAt soft-deletes the approver assignment. While set, the row
is treated as if the approver was never assigned.

layer.description:
Layer is the 0-indexed tier of this approver in the approval
chain. A layer may have multiple approvers (multiple rows sharing
the same setup_id and layer); any one of them acting is enough to
advance the timesheet to the next layer.

workspace_id.description: WorkspaceID is the workspace this approver's setup belongs to.

deleted_at.description:
DeletedAt soft-deletes the membership. While set, the row is treated
as if it didn't exist for membership checks.

discontinued_at.description:
DiscontinuedAt marks the member as discontinued: they keep their past
timesheets but are excluded from setup resolution, so no new periods
are generated for them. Nil means active; reactivation clears it.
Independent of DeletedAt (removal).

field, not this setting.

calendar_future_defaults_to_plan.description:
CalendarFutureDefaultsToPlan, when enabled, makes the unified-view event popover open future
slots in Plan time (past slots stay Log time). When disabled (default) the unified view
always opens in Log time. Does not affect the split view.

calendar_project_suggestion_fallback.description: CalendarProjectSuggestionFallback enables automatic project suggestion for newly-created calendar tasks.

calendar_task_creation_behavior.description: CalendarTaskCreationBehavior controls how calendar events map to tasks during sync.

first_interaction.description:
FirstInteraction determines the settings update was the first user interaction
done. This is what is used to dispatch the Focus product sign-up event. This
is not a setting that can be managed by FE. This is purely an internal BE
setting.

first_interaction_date.description:
FirstInteractionDate records when the user first interacted with Focus.
Set automatically by the BE alongside first_interaction.

goal_reminder_time.description: GoalReminderTime is the local clock time the daily goal reminder is sent, formatted HH:MM (24h).

goal_reminders_enabled.description: GoalRemindersEnabled opts the user into daily goal-reminder push notifications. Defaults to true.

has_reached_task_threshold.description: HasReachedTaskThreshold indicates the user has created 5+ tasks at some point.

onboarding_calendar_step_at.description: OnboardingCalendarStepAt is the ISO 8601 timestamp when the user left the calendar step (submitted or skipped)

onboarding_completed_at.description: OnboardingCompletedAt is the ISO 8601 timestamp when the user finished the onboarding flow

onboarding_started_at.description: OnboardingStartedAt is the ISO 8601 timestamp when the user first saw the onboarding page

onboarding_tasks_step_at.description: OnboardingTasksStepAt is the ISO 8601 timestamp when the user left the tasks step (submitted or skipped)

plan_tour_dismissed.description: PlanTourDismissed indicates whether the user has dismissed the plan onboarding tour

platform_nudges.description:
PlatformNudges maps a platform-discoverability nudge id to the ISO 8601 timestamp it was last
dismissed. Keys are opaque to the backend (nudge ids are owned by the web app), so new nudges
need no backend change. Absent/empty means nothing has been dismissed.

send_daily_brief.description:
SendDailyBrief opts the user into the morning Daily Brief email summarising yesterday's
tracked time and today's plan. Defaults to true.

send_timer_notifications.description:
SendTimerNotifications opts the user into the "timer still running" reminder email sent when
a timer has been left running for over 8 hours. Defaults to true.

show_goals_panel.description: ShowGoalsPanel controls whether the Goals panel is visible on the Timer page. Defaults to true.

start_week_on.description: StartWeekOn determines which day the week starts on: 0 for Sunday, 1 for Monday

features such as goal current-period detection. Mirrors the timezone stored in Toggl Track.

tooltip_onboarding_dismissed.description: TooltipOnboardingDismissed indicates whether the user has dismissed the tooltip onboarding tour

tos_ack_decoupled_licenses.description:
TosAckDecoupledLicenses maps an organization id to the ISO 8601 timestamp when
the user dismissed the seats-billing (decoupled-licenses) Terms-of-Service
announcement modal for that organization.

trial_ended_modal_seen.description:
TrialEndedModalSeen maps an organization id to the ISO 8601 timestamp when the user was
shown the end-of-trial modal for that organization. An absent entry for an org = not yet shown.

welcome_modal_dismissed.description: WelcomeModalDismissed indicates whether the user has dismissed the welcome modal

whats_new_may_2026_dismissed.description: WhatsNewMay2026Dismissed indicates whether the user has dismissed the May 2026 "What's new" tour

whats_new_tasks_tour_dismissed.description: WhatsNewTasksTourDismissed indicates whether the user has dismissed the tasks "What's new" tour

custom_field_values.description:
CustomFieldValues carries the member's user-level custom-field values.
Present only when the list is called with include_custom_fields=true on
a single workspace and the caller holds
view_workspace_user_custom_fields with the beta enabled; omitted
otherwise. Kept on this type (rather than a separate response type) so
the generated client's OrganizationUserResponse keeps its name — FE
code imports it directly.

is_truncated.description:
IsTruncated is true when the workspace has more than 5000 distinct projects across
the requested page of groups. Some groups may contain fewer projects than their total
indicates. Use projects_per_group with tighter filters to avoid truncation.

give feedback instead of rendering nothing.

target_group_id.description:
An explicit null target on a users-dimension move lands the task in
the no-assignee bucket (the id=0 group on reads) and enforces the

unchanged). Clearing
cannot depend on the source because an external drop (the

Moves in every other dimension require a real target — enforced in
the handler, where the dimension is known.

TimeEntries are the entries whose start falls in the period
(in the member's timezone), matching what is counted and what
can be flagged - not every entry overlapping the window. Each is
enriched with its task (name, tags) and project (name, color,

BillableMinutes is the sum of durations on entries marked
billable.

BillablePercent is BillableMinutes / TotalMinutes * 100,
rounded to one decimal place. Zero when TotalMinutes is
zero.

expected_minutes.description:
ExpectedMinutes is the working capacity for the period,
sourced from the capacity service.

logged_minutes.description:
LoggedMinutes equals TotalMinutes; kept as a separate field
so the planned-vs-logged comparison is self-documenting at
the call site.

planned_minutes.description:
PlannedMinutes is the sum of time block durations planned
for the period.

total_minutes.description: TotalMinutes is the sum of logged time entry durations.

align with the setup's anchor + periodicity.

being addressed (not the actor performing the action).

profile at query time. Not persisted with the timesheet.

name.description:

profile at query time. Not persisted with the timesheet, so it
always reflects the member's current name.

timesheet: the setup's configured approvers at the timesheet's

CapacityMinutes is the member's working-capacity minutes for the
period — the expected hours LoggedMinutes is measured against.

flag_count.description: FlagCount is the number of active flags on this timesheet.

LoggedMinutes is the sum of durations for entries whose start
falls in the period (in the member's timezone); an entry that
overlaps but starts in an adjacent period is not counted here.

member_name.description:
MemberName is the member's display name, resolved from their
account profile at query time. Not persisted with the timesheet,
so it always reflects the member's current name.

Reviews is the name-resolved review trail (actor, action, time),
oldest first, so the most recent entry is who last acted on the
timesheet. Empty for virtual rows.

timesheet.description: Timesheet is the underlying record (virtual or persisted).

default_for_levels.description:
DefaultForLevels lists every level this role is the default at, and is nil when it is not
one — never an empty list, which the stored column rejects.

require_group.description:
RequireGroup is true when the role is only conferred through a group, whatever Entity says.
Its permissions still cover Entity — a team role's cover the workspace — so a caller listing
the roles assignable directly at an entity has to drop the ones that carry it, while a
caller listing what a team can confer does not.

active_timesheet_setup_start_date.description:
ActiveTimesheetSetupStartDate is the start date of the setup the
caller is enrolled in, or null when they are not a member of one.
It anchors period computation on the client; the rest of the
setup is only needed by the admin management UI, which reads it
from the timesheet-setup list endpoint.

is_timesheet_approver.description:
IsTimesheetApprover reports whether the caller is assigned as an
approver on at least one active setup in this workspace.
